verdict: Tiingo EOD serves per-stock prices for delisted US names

probe_exceptions.EMC: ticker now owned by a different entity (ETF from 2023-05-15)

cross_validation_vs_independent_source.note: price LEVEL differs 1-5% because Tiingo applies CRSP split+DIVIDEND adjustment and the repo is split-only; the return PATH agrees to ~1bp MAE

free_tier_constraint.observed: budget spent after ~52 unique symbols on the free tier
free_tier_constraint.inferred_daily_cap: ~50 unique symbols/day (Tiingo docs claim 50; page is JS-rendered so UNVERIFIED)

ticker_reuse_hazard.statement: Tiingo's symbol master is keyed by ticker with one row per ticker, so it cannot represent reuse. /prices resolves to whichever entity owns the ticker NOW. The EMC master row is EMC Corp (1988-12-16..2016-09-15, correct) yet /prices returns a 2023 ETF. 3 of 45 tier-1 tickers affected.
ticker_reuse_hazard.mitigation: inline gate in the fetch: a series is accepted only if it stops within 3 days of the master's endDate, else quarantined to rejected_*.csv
ticker_reuse_hazard.why_it_matters: silent corruption -- a reused ticker injects a different asset's history into a dead-company slot: wrong prices AND look-ahead

blocking_question: is 40 large-cap deaths enough, or do we buy the full set?
